issue.description: Independent review of af3fe9c (2026-10-03). Repro (synthetic): postgres://worker:<A>%2F<B>%40<C>@localhost/db yields two overlapping uri-userinfo findings: raw view [18..56], normalized view [18..41] (the normalized view decodes %40 to @ and ends the userinfo there). Redacting the narrower fingerprint succeeds, leaves <C> stored, and doctor reports zero blocking because the marker's '[' makes the remainder look like a placeholder. Cause: structured_credentials.rs:82-100 checks raw bytes; spec 'Q(password, 8) after percent-decoding' not implemented. Fix: percent-decode userinfo before the qualifier; a decoded '@' must not end the userinfo in the normalized view; refuse or widen any selection strictly inside a same-rule finding. Note: 'bead redact --all-blocking' (a5134a5) already selects the covering finding, so it is not affected; explicit --finding selections are.
issue.notes: Implemented and pushed commit a414b4e (wip(beadrs-c43decfb): preserve encoded URI password ranges). URI credentials now parse userinfo with source-map provenance so a decoded %40 is included in the password until the raw @ delimiter; raw passwords are percent-decoded before Q(password, 8), and the full raw range is fingerprinted/redacted. Added a regression covering encoded %2F and %40 and asserting exactly one covering finding. A prior explicit narrow fingerprint can no longer be produced; stale retained selections are refused by redaction revalidation. Affected paths: src/scan/structured_credentials.rs, src/scan/mod.rs, tests/secret_gap_contract.rs. Verification: cargo test --test secret_gap_contract exit=0 (17 passed); cargo test --test redaction_transaction exit=0 (6 passed); cargo test --test redact_all_blocking exit=0 (2 passed); cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings exit=0; clean archive scripts/definition-of-done.sh --fast exit=0 (cargo fmt --check, cargo test: all tests and doctests passed); clean archive cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings exit=0; git push exit=0; git rev-list origin/main..HEAD empty. Workspace cargo fmt --check was attempted and reported only unrelated pre-existing worker formatting in tests/checkpoint_resilience.rs and tests/dependency_blocker_status.rs; task-owned files pass rustfmt --check. An initial invalid two-filter cargo test invocation was corrected by running each filter separately.

issue.description:
`bead query --help` advertises operators the implementation does not accept ('='), while the implemented grammar uses equals/contains operators and requires an explicit sort clause. The binary's own help is its primary API documentation and it actively misleads agents into issuing invalid queries. Update the clap help (and any capabilities/schema output that repeats the grammar) to match the implemented parser, add help-snapshot tests pinning the corrected text so it cannot drift again, and sweep README and research/specs for the same stale operator spellings.

Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Fix stale bead query help text: document the real operator and sort grammar
